title: WordPress development

seo.title: WordPress development company
seo.description: Custom WordPress and WooCommerce development without page-builder bloat: custom themes, structured content and fast pages. From $12,000.

answerBlock: WordPress development is building a website on WordPress with a custom theme and structured content, rather than stacking plugins onto a bought theme. Calwebtech builds lean WordPress and WooCommerce sites with custom post types, editor blocks that keep layouts intact and a written performance budget. Most marketing sites cost $12,000 to $25,000, and WooCommerce stores with integrations sit in the $25,000 to $60,000 band.

hero.outcome: A WordPress site that stays fast, keeps editors inside blocks they cannot break, and does not fall over every time a plugin updates.

problem.heading: When does a WordPress site need proper development?
problem.intro: WordPress is rarely the problem. How the site was put together usually is.

situations.title: Plugins are holding the site together
situations.body: Dozens of plugins overlap and conflict, updates are postponed because something breaks each time, and security patches wait with them.

situations.title: The page builder made everything slow
situations.body: Every page loads the builder's scripts and styles, mobile load times keep climbing, and editors can break a layout by dragging one block.

situations.title: Many sites, no shared system
situations.body: Separate WordPress installs for each location or brand drift apart, and one small change has to be made again and again.

included.heading: What is included in a WordPress build?
items: A custom theme built for your design system, with no page builder underneath
Custom post types and fields for services, case studies, locations and anything repeatable
Editor blocks designed for your content, with layouts editors cannot accidentally break
A short, audited plugin list, with each plugin justified in writing
WooCommerce set up with your pricing, shipping and tax rules, where you sell online
Multisite or shared components where several sites need to stay consistent
Forms that store every lead in your own database, with spam protection
A written performance budget, with image, script and caching work to meet it
WCAG 2.2 AA as the working standard
Hardening, updates tested on staging first and nightly encrypted backups
Editor training and a written operations manual

process.heading: How does a WordPress project run?
process.intro: Six to eight weeks for most sites. Multisite consolidations and WooCommerce stores with integrations take nine to fourteen.

steps.title: Audit and plan
steps.body: Content, plugins, speed and editing needs reviewed, then a content model, a plugin plan and a fixed scope agreed in writing.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: High-fidelity screens and the block library editors will use, approved before the theme is built.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Custom theme, post types, blocks and integrations on staging, with content migrated and redirects written as pages move.

steps.title: Prove
steps.body: Cross-browser and accessibility testing, a performance pass against the budget, a security review and a tested restore.

steps.title: Launch and hand over
steps.body: Cutover, monitoring, editor training and the operations manual, with updates tested on staging from the first day.

pricing.heading: How much does a WordPress website cost?
pricing.intro: Most WordPress marketing sites land between $12,000 and $25,000. WooCommerce stores with integrations, and multisite consolidations, sit in the $25,000 to $60,000 band.

factors.title: Content types
factors.body: Price follows distinct templates and post types, not page count.

factors.title: Migration

factors.title: WooCommerce

faq.heading: What do buyers ask about WordPress development?

items.question: Why not just buy a theme and a page builder?
items.answer: For a small site that rarely changes, that can be fine. Once the site carries many services, locations or case studies, a custom theme with structured content is faster, safer to edit and cheaper to keep running than a builder stacked with add-ons.

items.question: Can you rebuild our page-builder site without losing content?
items.answer: Yes. We migrate the content into structured post types and blocks, map every URL to its new address with permanent redirects, and check Search Console for the first thirty days after launch.

items.question: Do you build WooCommerce stores?
items.answer: Yes, including account-specific pricing, shipping and tax rules, and connections to inventory or ERP systems. If Shopify or a custom storefront would serve you better, we say so before you commit.

items.question: Can several of our sites run on one WordPress install?
items.answer: Yes. Multisite, or shared components across installs, lets locations or brands keep their own content while the design and code stay consistent. That is how fourteen clinic sites became one platform for one of our healthcare clients.

items.question: How do you keep WordPress secure?
items.answer: A short plugin list, updates tested on staging before production, hardened hosting, spam protection on forms, nightly encrypted backups and a tested restore. A month-to-month care plan keeps that running after launch.

items.question: Will our editors find it easy to use?
items.answer: They get blocks designed for your content, so they fill in the parts that change and cannot break the layout. Two recorded training sessions and a written manual come with every handover.

items.question: Should we use WordPress or Next.js?
items.answer: WordPress suits teams who know its editor and rely on its ecosystem. Next.js suits sites that need speed, custom logic or heavy integrations. WordPress can also run headless behind a Next.js front end, and the proposal explains which fits and why.
